name: Perform diagnostic imaging exams
summary: Medical radiation technologists, sonographers and nuclear medicine technologists perform about 24,000 X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, mammography and nuclear medicine exams a month across the corporation's three hospitals. Each exam starts when an emergency or inpatient order reaches the radiology worklist or a booked or walk-in outpatient checks in, and ends when the images are in PACS on the radiologist's reading list. The technologist identifies and screens the patient (pregnancy, contrast, MRI safety), positions and scans, and checks the images. The work is slowed by emergency orders that must be fitted around booked outpatients, waits for porters to bring inpatients, scanner and room capacity, incomplete requisitions and no-shows.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with about 640 beds, an emergency department at each site and a hospital-wide RIS, PACS and voice recognition system.
baseline.notes: Volumes from the corporation's annual reports; step times and branch shares are the author's estimates from general knowledge of Ontario hospital imaging, with the MRI scan duration and staffing, no-show rates and priority system from the Ontario Auditor General's 2018 audit. Wait times from order to scan for booked outpatients sit in dx-imaging-booking, not here.

trigger: An emergency or inpatient imaging order reaches the radiology worklist, or a booked or walk-in outpatient arrives at imaging reception with a requisition.
end_state: The images are stored in PACS and on the radiologist's reading worklist and the patient has left or been returned to the unit; or the exam is cancelled for rebooking or recorded as a no-show.

volume.seasonality: Fairly flat across the year with lower outpatient volumes in July, August and late December. Volumes fell in 2020/21 (250,235 exams) when non-urgent outpatient imaging was paused in the first COVID-19 wave, then rose to 298,482 in 2021/22.

evidence.note: 298,482 exams in 2021/22 (hh2122) is about 24,900 a month; the low and mode follow the organisation file's 2018/19 and 2020/21 figures from the same report series, which the author did not open.

surge.cause: Winter respiratory season and emergency department surges raise emergency and inpatient CT and X-ray demand

evidence.note: Author's estimate: emergency and inpatient exams are about half the volume, and ED visits rise about 10-20% in winter peaks.

Headcount 95 from the organisation file; about 52 FTE of hands-on exam work estimated from the simulated touch time, the rest on breaks, room preparation, QA, education and leave cover for 24/7 rotations.
Headcount 45; FTE on exams estimated from touch time; sonographers also spend time on worksheet completion, probe cleaning and room turnover not counted per exam.
Headcount 10; weekday service.

roles.title: Diagnostic imaging booking and reception clerk

evidence.note: Headcount 30 shared with dx-imaging-booking; reception, transport and no-show work estimated at about 8 FTE.
Protocolling, ultrasound checks and contrast reactions only; reading is in dx-radiology-reporting.
Share of porter time spent on imaging transports; also counted in fs-patient-portering.
Four managers across the sites; per-exam incident review only; scheduling and staffing work is not per case.
Oversight only; no per-case step.

systems.name: Hospital information system (electronic patient record with ADT, order entry, results, eMAR and clinical documentation)
Radiology information system, PACS and voice recognition dictation
Ontario Laboratories Information System and ConnectingOntario viewer
Fax (referrals, requisitions and reports to community physicians)
Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones
Safety incident and complaints reporting system

steps.name: Exam enters the modality worklist
steps.description: The order placed in the hospital information system, or the booked appointment for today, crosses the interface into the radiology information system and appears on the modality worklist with its priority (stat, urgent or routine), patient location and requisition image.

error.defect_description: Interface drops or duplicates an order, or the order carries the wrong exam code.

next.condition: outpatient (booked, walk-in or fracture clinic) arrives at reception

evidence.note: Split of 52% outpatient and 48% emergency or inpatient exams is the author's estimate from the corporation's volumes: about 13,000 ED visits a month (hh2122) with roughly 45% imaged, about 4,000 inpatient exams, 2,000 fracture clinic exams and the rest booked or walk-in outpatients. No-show share of 2% of all exams applies the low-to-middle of the 0.1-13.4% MRI and 0.6-13% CT no-show ranges in oag2018 to the booked share only.

steps.name: Check in outpatient and verify the requisition
steps.description: The imaging reception clerk takes the paper or faxed requisition, confirms the patient has been registered, checks that the requisition is signed by an authorised practitioner and names the exam and clinical question, and marks the patient arrived in the radiology system.

error.defect_description: Arrives the wrong exam or a second order for the same exam.

control.basis: Healing Arts Radiation Protection Act (Ontario): X-ray exams only on the order of a physician or other authorised practitioner

next.condition: requisition unsigned, illegible or missing the clinical question

evidence.note: Reception check-in steps are the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospital imaging departments; times are estimates.

steps.name: Phone the ordering office to complete the requisition
steps.description: The clerk phones or faxes the ordering physician's office for a signature, the missing clinical history or a corrected exam, while the patient waits in reception; if no one answers the patient is sent home and rebooked.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Share and waits are the author's estimate; oag2018 reports that hospitals did not consistently check that referrals were appropriate, but gives no incomplete-requisition rate.

steps.name: Fit the emergency or inpatient exam into the schedule
steps.description: The charge or modality technologist looks at the worklist, ranks emergency and stat orders above inpatient routine orders and the booked outpatients already in the rooms, and decides when the exam can be done and whether the patient must be brought down or imaged at the bedside.

error.defect_description: A stat order is missed on a long worklist and waits behind routine work.

next.condition: patient must be brought by porter
patient too unwell to move: portable exam
emergency patient walks or is wheeled over by ED staff

evidence.note: Author's estimate. The organisation file describes emergency and inpatient exams being fitted around booked outpatients, with CT demand from the ED and porter availability driving queues.

steps.name: Request a porter for the inpatient
steps.description: The imaging clerk enters a transport request in the portering system or phones dispatch, giving the patient's unit, bed, mode (stretcher, wheelchair, bed) and isolation status, and phones the unit so nursing can prepare the patient.

error.defect_description: Wrong isolation status or transport mode on the request.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on common practice in Ontario community hospitals.

steps.name: Porter brings the patient to imaging
steps.description: A porter collects the patient from the inpatient unit or emergency stretcher, checks the armband against the request, moves the patient by stretcher or wheelchair to the imaging sub-waiting area and hands over to the technologist.

error.defect_description: Wrong patient collected or chart left behind.

control.basis: Accreditation Canada required organizational practice on client identification: two identifiers before a service

evidence.note: Porter labour is also counted in fs-patient-portering; it is shown here because the wait for a porter is one of the main delays in inpatient imaging (organisation file description).

steps.name: Take the portable X-ray unit to the bedside
steps.description: The technologist collects a portable X-ray unit, checks its battery and detector, and wheels it through the corridors and elevators to the intensive care unit, emergency resuscitation bay or ward where the patient cannot be moved.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate. Portable units are not listed in the organisation file resources and are added here.

steps.name: Perform the portable exam at the bedside
steps.description: The technologist confirms the patient's identity from the armband with the nurse, clears bystanders or hands out lead aprons, positions the detector behind the patient with help from nursing, exposes the image and checks it on the unit's screen before sending it to PACS.

error.defect_description: Rotated or under-penetrated film, or tube or line not fully shown.

control.basis: Hospital radiation protection program under the Healing Arts Radiation Protection Act: shielding and clearing staff before exposure

evidence.note: Author's estimate of portable chest X-ray time in a community hospital.

steps.name: Wait for the room or scanner to come free
steps.description: The patient waits in the department sub-waiting area or on a stretcher until the X-ray room, CT or MRI scanner, ultrasound room or nuclear medicine camera finishes the case ahead; emergency and stat patients are slotted in between booked outpatients.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Modality mix (about 58% radiography including portables, 16% CT, 5% MRI, 19% ultrasound, 3% nuclear medicine) is the author's estimate for a large Ontario community hospital; oag2018 confirms emergency scans were over 30% of CT in Ontario in 2017/18.

steps.name: Identify and screen the X-ray patient
steps.description: The technologist calls the patient in, confirms name and date of birth against the requisition and armband, asks women of child-bearing age about pregnancy, checks the clinical question against the views ordered and has the patient change into a gown if needed.

error.defect_description: Wrong patient or wrong side not caught.

control.basis: Accreditation Canada required organizational practice on client identification: two identifiers before a service

evidence.note: Standard technologist checks; author's general knowledge of Ontario MRT practice.

steps.name: Position the patient and take the radiographs
steps.description: The technologist positions the patient for each view, places the side marker, collimates, makes the exposures, checks each image on the console for positioning and exposure and repeats a view that is not diagnostic, then enters the exam as complete with any notes.

error.defect_description: Missing view, wrong side marker or a repeat that adds dose.

control.basis: Healing Arts Radiation Protection Act and hospital radiation safety program: collimation, shielding, dose records

evidence.note: Author's estimate; retake rate of about 3% is an estimate for digital radiography.

steps.name: Screen the CT patient for contrast and start the IV
steps.description: The CT technologist confirms identity, checks the protocol on the order, asks about contrast allergy, diabetes medication and kidney disease, looks up the latest creatinine or eGFR in the lab results, and inserts an intravenous line when contrast is planned.

error.defect_description: Contrast given despite low eGFR or unrecorded allergy.

control.basis: Hospital contrast administration policy and medical directive: renal function and allergy screening before iodinated contrast

next.condition: no protocol yet or contrast question for the radiologist

evidence.note: Author's estimate of share of ED and inpatient CT needing a radiologist protocol at scan time.

steps.name: Radiologist sets the CT protocol
steps.description: The radiologist reads the order and clinical history on the worklist, chooses the scan protocol (region, phases, contrast or not) or approves contrast for a patient with a borderline kidney result or prior reaction, and records it in the radiology system.

error.defect_description: Protocol misses a phase needed to answer the clinical question.

control.basis: Radiologist responsibility for the imaging protocol and contrast decision (CPSO and hospital medical staff rules)

evidence.note: oag2018 states radiologists assess requisitions and determine the type of scan and priority; the share and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Scan the patient on CT
steps.description: The technologist positions the patient on the CT table, runs the scout images, sets the scan range, starts the contrast injector when required, watches the patient through the window, checks the reconstructed images and removes the IV after the observation period.

error.defect_description: Motion or contrast timing makes part of the scan non-diagnostic.

control.basis: Healing Arts Radiation Protection Act and hospital dose protocols for CT

evidence.note: Author's estimate of CT room time; contrast reaction share is an estimate.

steps.name: Screen the MRI patient for safety
steps.description: The MRI technologist goes through the MRI safety questionnaire with the patient (pacemakers, implants, metal fragments, pregnancy, claustrophobia), looks up implant cards or prior reports, removes metal objects and decides whether the patient may enter the magnet room.

error.defect_description: Unsafe implant missed.

control.basis: MRI safety screening before entry to the magnet room (hospital MRI safety policy, Accreditation Canada diagnostic imaging standards)

next.condition: contraindication or claustrophobia: cancelled and rebooked

evidence.note: Author's estimate; share cancelled at screening is an estimate.

steps.name: Scan the patient on MRI
steps.description: Two technologists position the patient with the right coil, give hearing protection, run the sequences from the protocol, inject gadolinium when ordered, watch the patient on camera and check the images before taking the patient out of the magnet.

error.defect_description: Motion artefact or wrong coil gives a non-diagnostic sequence.

evidence.note: oag2018: an MRI scan with contrast takes on average 40 minutes and needs at least two technologists on site; other scans take about 20 minutes. people=2 assumes the hospital staffs two per scanner.

steps.name: Perform the ultrasound
steps.description: The sonographer confirms identity, reviews the requisition and prior reports, scans the region with the protocol views and measurements, saves images to PACS and fills in the worksheet of findings for the radiologist.

error.defect_description: Incomplete views or measurements that the radiologist needs.

control.basis: Accreditation Canada required organizational practice on client identification

next.condition: sonographer asks the radiologist to check before the patient leaves

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a general ultrasound slot in an Ontario hospital.

steps.name: Radiologist checks the ultrasound images while the patient waits
steps.description: The radiologist opens the images and worksheet on a reading station, decides whether the exam answers the question, and either releases the patient or asks for more views, sometimes scanning briefly themselves.
outputs: release or request for more views

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice in Canadian ultrasound departments.

steps.name: Prepare and inject the radiopharmaceutical
steps.description: The nuclear medicine technologist confirms identity and pregnancy or breastfeeding status, draws up the prescribed radiopharmaceutical dose from the hot lab, measures it in the dose calibrator, injects it and records the lot and activity.

error.defect_description: Wrong dose or wrong radiopharmaceutical drawn up.

control.basis: Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission licence conditions for nuclear substances: dose measurement and records

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Image the patient on the gamma camera after uptake
steps.description: After the uptake period the technologist positions the patient on the camera, acquires the planar or SPECT images, checks them for motion and completeness and processes the study before sending it to PACS.

error.defect_description: Motion or incomplete acquisition.

evidence.note: Uptake times of one to three hours are typical of bone and other scans; author's estimate.

steps.name: Treat a contrast reaction
steps.description: When a patient reacts to contrast, the technologist stops the injection and calls the radiologist, who assesses the patient, gives antihistamine, steroid or epinephrine from the reaction kit as needed, and arranges transfer to the emergency department if the reaction is severe.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Manager reviews the reaction incident report
steps.description: The imaging manager reads the incident report filed after the reaction, checks that the allergy has been added to the patient's record and the reaction kit restocked, and decides whether the event needs wider review.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Accreditation Canada standards on patient safety incident management

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the study to PACS and the reading worklist
steps.description: When the technologist completes the exam, the radiology system matches the images to the accession number, stores them in PACS and places the study on the radiologist's reading worklist with its priority.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: images and order do not match

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Fix a mismatched or broken study in RIS and PACS
steps.description: The lead technologist works through the PACS exceptions list, matches orphan images to the right accession, merges studies sent under a duplicate order or moves images filed to the wrong patient, and tells the radiologist when a read report is affected.

error.defect_description: Images moved to the wrong study.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; there is no PACS administrator role in the organisation file, so the lead MRT does this.

steps.name: Request return transport
steps.description: The imaging clerk enters a return transport request for the inpatient or stretcher patient and phones the unit to say the patient is on the way back.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Porter returns the patient to the unit
steps.description: A porter collects the patient from the imaging holding area, checks the armband, returns the patient to the unit or emergency department and hands over to the nurse, while the patient waits on a stretcher in imaging until then.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; labour also counted in fs-patient-portering.

steps.name: Mark the no-show and notify booking
steps.description: After the grace period the reception clerk marks the booked appointment as a no-show in the radiology system, tries to fill the slot with a waiting emergency or inpatient case, and leaves the order on the booking list for rebooking.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: oag2018 reports no-show rates of 0.1-13.4% for MRI and 0.6-13% for CT and that hospitals could fill CT slots with little difficulty; times are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Incomplete requisition
exceptions.description: The outpatient's requisition is unsigned or lacks the clinical question; the clerk phones the ordering office and 15% of these patients go home to rebook.

exceptions.name: Portable exam at the bedside
exceptions.description: Critically ill or isolated patients are imaged with a portable unit, taking the technologist away from the department.

exceptions.name: Contrast reaction
exceptions.description: A patient reacts to iodinated or gadolinium contrast; the radiologist treats the patient and the manager reviews the incident.

exceptions.name: Study mismatch
exceptions.description: Images arrive in PACS without a matching order or under the wrong accession and must be corrected before or after reading.

exceptions.name: MRI contraindication
exceptions.description: Safety screening finds an unsafe implant or the patient cannot tolerate the scanner; the exam is cancelled and rebooked, sometimes with sedation.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the order reaching the worklist (or outpatient arrival) to images on the reading worklist
benchmarks.population: All exams in an Ontario community hospital, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 45-75 minutes from arrival to images for outpatients, one to two hours from order for emergency patients and several hours for routine inpatient exams. Ontario publishes waits from order to scan only for booked MRI and CT (hsi_di), not door-to-image times.

benchmarks.value: order received date to scan date, average and 90th percentile

evidence.note: Used to set the boundary between dx-imaging-booking (waiting for the scan) and this process.

pain_points.description: Emergency CT and X-ray orders interrupt booked outpatient lists, so booked patients wait and inpatient routine exams slip to the evening or next day.

evidence.note: oag2018 reports emergency scans were more than 30% of CT and that emergency demand leaves less machine time for other priority levels.

pain_points.description: Inpatients wait for porters both ways, and the scanner may sit idle while a booked inpatient is late.

evidence.note: Author's general knowledge; the organisation file names porter availability as a main driver of queues.

pain_points.description: No-shows waste MRI time that is hard to fill at short notice; phone reminders confirm far fewer patients than text messages.

evidence.note: 48,320 missed MRI appointments in Ontario in 2017/18; 25-36% confirmation after phone reminders versus 50% after texts.

pain_points.description: Scanners are funded for limited hours, so capacity rather than staff time sets the wait for CT and MRI.

evidence.note: 69% of Ontario's 108 MRI machines ran below 16 hours a day, seven days a week in 2017/18 because hospitals could not fund more hours.

sources.title: 2018 Annual Report, Volume 1, Chapter 3, Section 3.08: MRI and CT Scanning Services
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Ministry priority levels for MRI and CT: emergency (P1, within 24 hours), urgent (P2, within 2 days), semi-urgent (P3, within 10 days), non-urgent (P4, within 28 days), targets set at the 90th percentile; before booking, radiologists assess the requisition, determine the type of scan and assign a priority, then a scheduler books a predefined slot; an MRI scan with contrast takes on average 40 minutes and needs at least two technologists on site, other MRI scans about 20 minutes with one; emergency scans were more than 30% of CT scans in 2017/18; MRI no-show rates 0.1% to 13.4% and CT 0.6% to 13% of scheduled appointments in 2017/18 (48,320 missed MRI and 57,916 missed CT appointments); 25-36% of patients confirmed after phone reminders versus 50% after text messages; studies found 6% to 12% of scans inappropriate under CAR referral guidelines; peer review of radiologist reports was not mandatory and three of four audited hospitals had a regular program; 69% of MRI machines ran below 16 hours a day, seven days a week; 65% of semi-urgent and non-urgent MRI patients and 33% of CT patients waited longer than target in 2017/18

sources.title: 2021-2022 Annual Community Report (Halton Healthcare by the numbers)
sources.supports: 2021/22: 298,482 diagnostic imaging exams, 161,049 emergency visits, 45,256 surgeries, 4,690 births, 37,964 dialysis visits, 19,600 oncology visits, 62,508 mental health and addictions ambulatory visits, 40,428 fracture clinic visits, 3,220,658 laboratory tests, 5,228 staff, 931 physicians, dentists and midwives

sources.title: About the Diagnostic Imaging Wait Times Dashboard
sources.publisher: Ontario Health (Health System Information help pages)
sources.supports: Ontario MRI and CT wait times run from the date the order is received to the scan date and are reported as an average and a 90th percentile, by priority, with scans counted within or over target

assumptions: The case starts when the order is on the worklist (emergency and inpatient) or when the outpatient arrives; the weeks a booked outpatient waits for a CT or MRI slot belong to dx-imaging-booking.
Modality mix is estimated (radiography and mammography 58%, CT 16%, MRI 5%, ultrasound 19%, nuclear medicine 3%); mammography is folded into the radiography path and fluoroscopy into the X-ray rooms.

The step graph is memoryless: after the shared send-to-PACS step, return transport is drawn at 25% for all cases rather than only for those brought by porter. This slightly understates porter work for inpatients and overstates it for outpatients.

Interface share of 19% from primary_care (walk-in outpatient X-ray and ultrasound with a community requisition) is not in the organisation file's triggers for this process; it is added because Ontario community hospitals take walk-in general X-ray. fs-patient-portering's transported_patient is a hand-off inside the case, not a trigger, so it is not listed in triggered_by.
Portable X-ray units are not listed in the organisation file's resources; eight are assumed across three sites.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage times 1.35). Porter labour also appears in fs-patient-portering.

Simulated median cycle time is about 0.09 days (2.2 hours), 1.5 times the tier C benchmark of 0.06 days. The gap comes from emergency and inpatient cases, which wait on the worklist and for porters both ways; the step graph adds the return trip to elapsed time although the images are in PACS before the patient leaves. Simulated hands-on time implies about 108 FTE against 94 FTE stated; the stated figure is kept because porter and radiologist minutes are mostly counted in other processes.
